cards.title: Publish wallet events on ledger change, not after every actor message
shared_surfaces: table-ledger public API (one read-only accessor, Ledger::write_count, over rusqlite Connection::total_changes; no raw SQL crosses)
acceptance: Spawned actor over a counting vault, 2 open deals, interval tick held (paused tokio clock): 100 `get_deal` Execute messages -> 0 vault reads in total (today every message runs the publish pass: settings() alone reads the keychain 3 times, forecast() calls settings() again plus owner() per open deal, envelope_view() once, so >= 900 reads)

Same actor: `deal_withdraw` on deal A -> exactly one WalletEvent::Deal for A (state Withdrawn) and one WalletEvent::Attention are received before the reply to the next message (unchanged latency for writes)

`deal_reconcile` (authority tier Read, but it writes and moves A to Reconciled) -> WalletEvent::Deal and WalletEvent::Receipt for A are still published: the trigger is the ledger write count, never the command's tier

A Message::Agent `table_view` intent for a live run -> no publish pass (vault reads equal those of calling Runtime::agent_intent directly); a `send_offer` that is accepted -> one WalletEvent::Deal for the deal (transcript head moved)
A native run streams 50 EngineEvent::Text messages -> 0 publish passes (vault read count unchanged); EngineFinished(Clean) -> one WalletEvent::Agent with state Clean
Internal Action::HouseStatus(Ready) (no ledger write, in-memory settings change) -> one WalletEvent::Settings with house = Ready published immediately
FinishUnlock after a verified re-auth -> one WalletEvent::Settings with locked = false published without waiting for the 1 s tick
With the interval running and no message, a deal whose deadline passes is still published within one tick (the tick always runs the pass, as today)
premise: crates/table-runtime/src/actor.rs:461 - every Message::Execute runs runtime.execute and then falls through to the post-select publish pass

crates/table-runtime/src/actor.rs:480-554 - the publish pass runs after EVERY message: list_deals and two JSON serialisations per deal (483-484), attention() (534), settings() (538), run_snapshots() (545)
crates/table-runtime/src/actor.rs:467,469 - Agent intents and every streamed engine event are messages, so each one also triggers the full pass
crates/table-runtime/src/engines.rs:260-273 - every engine event of a run is forwarded to the actor as Message::Engine
crates/table-runtime/src/dispatcher.rs:209-252 - attention() reads money_check, two preferences, display_number, deadline and needs_owner_accept per deal
crates/table-runtime/src/dispatcher.rs:261,273,278 - attention() also folds exposure (envelope_view), builds the forecast and writes ladder rungs

crates/table-runtime/src/forecast.rs:24 - forecast() calls settings() again; forecast.rs:53 mandate_retired per open deal; forecast.rs:61 select_signer per seller deal; forecast.rs:126-151 a binary search of step_allowed calls per settling seller deal
crates/table-runtime/src/service.rs:338-352 - settings() reads the OS keychain for paypal.sandbox and channel3 and the owner key on every call
crates/table-runtime/src/service.rs:292,315 - mandate_retired reads the owner key; select_agent reads up to three agent keys
crates/table-runtime/src/vault.rs:67-84 - KeyringVault::read goes to the Windows credential store on every call (no cache)
crates/table-client/src/authority_table.rs:209 - deal_reconcile is tier Read although it writes, so tier cannot be the publish signal
crates/table-ledger/src/lib.rs:51-55 - Ledger owns the single rusqlite Connection the actor writes through (no raw SQL crosses)
docs/build/SCALE-FINDINGS.md:72 - open: about 300 displays re-read after any ledger change at scale; each such read is one actor message
docs/build/DECISIONS.md:1396-1398 - the rebuild rejected batched read commands; per-deal reads at 500+ deals stay many small reads
cards.rollback: Three commits (ledger accessor, actor publish gate, tests); revert in reverse order. The gate is one condition in the actor loop, and reverting it restores the publish-after-every-message behaviour exactly. No schema, IPC or binding change.
cards.runner_up: Resolve the deal's agent signer per call inside table-app and delete Runtime::select_signer plus Pipeline's signer_missing / shield_refused / policy_paused side-channel flags (25 select_signer/select_agent call sites across 10 runtime files). It spans table-app, so it is close to XL.
cards.adopts: docs/build/SCALE-FINDINGS.md open item (#17 and WP1b 1: per-deal read cost at scale); not a moonshot card
cards.body:
## Summary
The actor recomputes and diffs the whole wallet after every message it handles, including pure reads, read-only agent tools and each streamed engine event. Run that pass only when the ledger write count moved, when in-memory published state changed, or on the 1 s tick. Today a read costs O(N deals), and a fan-out of N reads costs O(N^2).

## Description
`run()` in actor.rs ends each loop turn with a publish pass. The pass lists every deal and JSON-diffs it, builds the attention snapshot (per-deal ledger reads, exposure fold, the walk-away forecast with its binary search, rung writes), rebuilds settings (3 OS keychain reads plus a signature check over all mandates) and diffs the run snapshots. The pass is right for the tick and for writes, but it also runs after every `get_deal`, `deal_display` and `deal_evidence`. The client's own scale work (readEach.ts, displays.ts, SCALE-FINDINGS #17 and WP1b 1) is a workaround for this multiplier, and DECISIONS section 40.6 accepted many small reads as the known limit.

The move: add `Ledger::write_count()` (rusqlite `total_changes`, already in 0.38), read on the actor's own connection. The loop publishes when (a) the tick fired, (b) `write_count` advanced since the last pass (this catches `deal_reconcile`, rung writes, preferences, run.start/finish rows and offers), or (c) the message changed in-memory published state with no ledger write (FinishUnlock, HouseStatus, Engine Init/Finished: an explicit `dirty` flag on Runtime). The count is taken after the pass, so the pass's own rung writes do not re-trigger it. The ground truth is the database, not a hand-kept list of which commands write. The tier is not used, because `deal_reconcile` is tier Read and writes. A missed in-memory flag self-heals at the next tick (at most 1 s late), which bounds the risk.

## Flow
- Ledger: `pub fn write_count(&self) -> u64 { self.conn.total_changes() }`
- Runtime: `published_at: u64`, `publish_dirty: bool` (service.rs)
- actor.rs: extract the pass into `publish(&mut runtime, &events, &mut caches)`, call it on the tick, or when `write_count() != published_at || publish_dirty`, then record `published_at` after it
- FinishUnlock, HouseStatus and engine Init/Finished set `publish_dirty`
- publish_tests.rs: a CountingVault (implements the pub Vault trait) and a held tokio clock; each test names its negative control (registry test-harness: drop the gate and case 1 fails; gate on tier and case 3 fails)

## Expected impact
- An IPC read does no hidden whole-wallet work: 0 keychain reads instead of >= 9 + N_open per read.
- A 300-display or 500-evidence fan-out costs O(N), not O(N^2), with no IPC change, so it stays inside the 40.6 freeze rationale.
- A native run's text stream no longer recomputes the forecast per chunk.
- The Tumbler and main still see writes at once and time-driven changes within 1 s.

## Evaluation
Claim: post-message publication is the multiplier behind the per-read cost at scale, and change-gating it keeps every event a write produces.
Before: 0 of 8 acceptance cases pass as tests: case 1 counts >= 900 vault reads. Cases 2, 3, 6, 7 and 8 hold today but are not pinned. Cases 4 and 5 run a pass.
After: 8 of 8 (predicted)
Method: simulation - walked actor.rs:458-555 for a get_deal, a deal_reconcile (writes, tier Read), a table_view intent, an EngineEvent::Text, HouseStatus and FinishUnlock; counted keychain reads in settings/forecast/envelope_view/mandate_retired; the gate rung is the builder's
Result: better
Gate: none - internal publication timing. No IPC, authority, schema or money-path change; the tick keeps its every-second pass.

cards.title: Resume shows the tables waiting on your agent and restarts them in one click
shared_surfaces: CommandContract (resume_all_agents output type; authority row unchanged)
acceptance: Seller deal A Negotiating, last message an inbound OFFER, policy run live; Pause then Resume -> resume_all_agents returns ResumeReport { waiting: [A] } (today it returns null, so the decode into ResumeReport fails)

Deal B whose latest step is our own COUNTER (projection turn = theirs) -> B is not in waiting; deal C with our turn but `lapse.C` chosen -> not in waiting; deal D terminal (Withdrawn) -> not in waiting
Deal E whose turn is ours but with a live run -> not in waiting; deal F whose turn is ours but whose deadline has passed -> not in waiting

waiting lists one entry per deal, ordered by deadline ascending, each { deal_id, deadline }. Membership is exactly AgentProjection.allowed containing send_offer or accept_offer, the same predicate the wallet enforces (table-core agent.rs:310-323)

Resume starts nothing by itself (explicit-start rule kept): with the scripted engine, 3 ticks after Resume give runs.len() == 0 for A. agent_start(A) (the Restart click) gives one run, and that run sends exactly one COUNTER envelope for A
Client restartPlan(waiting=[A,B,C,D,E], running=1, cap=4) -> { start: [A,B,C], later: [D,E] }; restartPlan([], 0, 4) -> { start: [], later: [] }

Client: after Resume with a non-empty report, the Agents view offers 'Restart N tables' and calls agent_start once per id in plan.start, in order. A refused start (run limit) is reported per table and never retried in a loop

cards.body:
## Summary
Pause is the wallet's kill switch. Resume clears the flag and then says 'Start each deal yourself'. It does not say which deals: the owner hunts through the deal pages for the tables that were mid-haggle. A table cut mid-turn stalls silently until its deadline lapses it. The policy negotiator never re-arms on a transcript head whose run was cancelled (policy.rs:128), although a relaunch would re-arm it. The wallet already knows exactly which tables are waiting on our agent, from the same `allowed` predicate it enforces. Resume should return that list, and the owner should restart them in one click.

## Description
`resume_all_agents` returns `ResumeReport { waiting: Vec<WaitingTable { deal_id, deadline }> }`. It is computed in Rust by `Runtime::waiting_on_agent(now)` over non-terminal Haggle deals with no live run, no `lapse.<id>`, an active mandate and a deadline in the future, whose `Wallet::projection(..).allowed` contains `send_offer` or `accept_offer`. It is derived from ground truth, not a hand-kept 'interrupted' list, so the same report covers runs cut by Pause, by Quit (after relaunch) or by a failed or expired run. The explicit-start rule (STATUS 1068) is kept: Resume starts nothing. In the Agents view, the owner sees 'N tables are waiting on your agent', soonest deadline first, and one 'Restart N' action that calls the existing agent_start per table through a pure `restartPlan` that respects the 4-run cap. No authority row, capability or manifest changes; only one command's output type changes.

## Flow
- Owner presses Pause (P, tray or Tumbler): runs cancelled, deadlines still run
- Owner presses Resume: the report comes back, and the Agents view lists the waiting tables with their deadlines
- One click 'Restart 3 tables': agent_start x3 (cap 4); '2 wait for a free slot' shows when over the cap
- Each restarted policy run answers the pending OFFER or COUNTER once; native runs start from their playbook

## Expected impact
- The kill switch becomes reversible in one step instead of N deal-page visits.
- The silent stall after Pause and Resume (a table that lapses with nobody answering) becomes a visible, one-click decision.
- The 'pause, then resume' demo beat ends with the haggle continuing on camera.

## Evaluation
Claim: the owner's resume decision is made blind today, although Rust holds the exact predicate. Returning it makes resume a one-step act and keeps the explicit-start rule.
Before: 0 of 7 acceptance cases pass (resume returns null; restartPlan does not exist). Case 5's 'Resume starts nothing' half holds today.
After: 7 of 7 (predicted)
Method: simulation - walked Pause (dispatcher.rs:675-684) -> cancel_runs -> Resume (550-558) -> tick -> arm_policy_run (policy.rs:122-139, early return at 128) for a seller deal with an inbound OFFER; walked projection.allowed for own-COUNTER, lapse-chosen, terminal and live-run deals; the gate rung is the builder's
Result: better
Gate: contract - resume_all_agents output type (in-repo CommandContract plus generated bindings and the mock). Authority row, tiers and PINNED_MANIFEST unchanged. DECISIONS 40.6 froze IPC for the console rebuild only; that rebuild has landed, but the coordinator should confirm the freeze has lifted.

riders.checked: Read table-mcp lib.rs and table-shield lib.rs in full. Tested two hypotheses: tool names hand-kept in 4 places (core AgentTool, mcp Tool + catalog, engine parser TOOLS, app AgentRequest::decode), and DISPATCH_DEADLINE 30 s against an actor that can sit up to ~183 s in a PayPal step. The first is guarded by drift tests (server.rs:1002), so impact < 7. The second is the actor's problem and folds into the host's 'PayPal IO inside the actor' idea (XL).

Read table-market lib.rs and runtime market.rs. Market-watch refresh (T15) and the fair-price certificate (market-data-2) are built. The one gap seen: market_refresh makes the client echo a product_id that Rust already derives (market.rs:110-131), which is S polish, not a card.

Read agent.rs, negotiation.rs and checks.rs in full; exposure, market_watch, ladder and rescue headers only. These are pure and well bounded, and T14, T5, agent-tool-surface-1 and T2 are built. Card B reuses AgentProjection.allowed as its ground truth instead of adding a new predicate.

never_repropose_checked: Ruled out as overlaps: T2 negotiator (built; card B adds no re-arm rule), T4 walk-away forecast and quit confirm (built), T11 authority manifest (card A deliberately does not derive from tier), T16 ledger-2 verified projection (different: audit deltas, not event publication), T3 attested engine session (gated), incidental runtime-core scheduler.rs:57 Fault-per-second (now mandate_retired-guarded), and the SCALE-FINDINGS batched-read command (rejected in DECISIONS 40.6; card A needs no IPC).
